clue.text: Tumbledown lamasery -a fake ruin — in a Conrad book

indicators.note: a tumbledown building has collapsed, so the letters of lamasery fall into a new order

parts.note: a folly is a sham ruin built to decorate a landscape garden

explanation.surface: A ruined monastery turns out to be a mock ruin in a Joseph Conrad novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbledown' rearranges LAMASERY into ALMAYERS; a folly is an ornamental building made to look old, often as a fake ruin. Almayer's Folly was Conrad's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Almayer's Folly (1895) is the first novel Joseph Conrad published.

clue.text: Eponymous daughter of the Potteries

parts.note: the heroine of Arnold Bennett's novel named after her, set in the Staffordshire pottery towns

explanation.walkthrough: The Potteries is the Staffordshire area around Stoke-on-Trent, Arnold Bennett's Five Towns; the heroine of Anna of the Five Towns is the miser's daughter whose name is in the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Bennett's novel Anna of the Five Towns is named after its heroine, the daughter of a miser in the Staffordshire pottery district.

clue.text: Those in Luzhin's Defence led to his

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Those in Luzhin's Defence led to his' with no letter count: cut off after 'his', and a search of the exact text did not find the rest
annotationWithheld.clue: Those in Luzhin's Defence led to his

clue.text: Cowardly defender of the railway novel

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A timid footballer stands up for cheap paperback fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellowbacks were cheap Victorian novels in yellow board covers, sold at railway station bookstalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowbacks were cheap Victorian novels with yellow covers, sold to travellers at station bookstalls.

clue.text: Concerning list behind altar

definitions.note: a phrase saying where the thing stands, defining a noun for a structure placed there

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a business letter
a table is a list of figures or facts, such as a league table

explanation.surface: A note about a list kept at the back of a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A retable is a shelf or decorated panel set up at the back of a church's communion table.

clue.text: A fee run specially for American poet

indicators.note: done specially, made in a new way, so the letters of a fee run are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charge is levied for an event staged for a visiting American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Freneau (1752-1832) was a poet of the American Revolution.

clue.text: Hofmannsthal's was not a biography

parts.note: the Austrian writer adapted Calderón's play about existence being only a dream, so his version of a person's story was no biography

explanation.walkthrough: Hugo von Hofmannsthal reworked Calderón's play La vida es sueño (Life is a Dream), so his 'life' was a dream, not someone's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Hofmannsthal adapted Calderón's Life is a Dream, a play whose title word normally names the subject of a biography.

clue.text: … and he wrote this twenty-four hours ago

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 6-down: Hofmannsthal also wrote the early verse play Gestern, German for the day before today.
explanation.definitionFit: Hofmannsthal wrote the play Gestern, whose title translates the word; it also means on the day before today.

clue.text: Dickensian evangelist right always to terminate schoolboy mistake

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
to end means to terminate
a howler is a glaring blunder, typically a pupil's

explanation.surface: A Dickens preacher is always right to put an end to children's blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reverend Melchisedech Howler is the ranting preacher in Dickens's Dombey and Son.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reverend Melchisedech Howler is a ranting preacher in Dickens's Dombey and Son.

clue.text: A little fiction

parts.note: reads as a small lie, but means a short work of prose storytelling

explanation.definitionFit: A short novel, longer than a short story, is given the diminutive ending of its parent form.

clue.text: Clown is second in gala

indicators.note: the letter for second goes in the middle of the word for gala

parts.note: a fete is a festive gala

explanation.surface: A clown comes second at the summer fete.
explanation.walkthrough: Feste is the jester in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Feste is the jester, or fool, in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Rotas sort of rearranged to include poet/dramatist

indicators.note: the words rotas sort include the run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Duty schedules shuffled to fit in a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'roTAS SOrt'. Torquato Tasso was the Italian author of Jerusalem Delivered and the play Aminta.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso (1544-95) wrote the epic Jerusalem Delivered and the pastoral drama Aminta.

clue.text: Harris's brother

parts.note: the dialect word for brother used in Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus tales, as in the rabbit and the fox

explanation.walkthrough: Joel Chandler Harris wrote the Uncle Remus stories, whose animals are titled by the dialect word for brother: Rabbit and Fox.
explanation.definitionFit: In Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus stories the animal characters carry this dialect form of 'brother'.

clue.text: Venerable Eliot protagonist

explanation.surface: A respected main character in a George Eliot novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon historian is known as the Venerable one; Adam, the carpenter, is the title hero of George Eliot's first novel.

clue.text: Clare proud, perhaps, following routine

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of clare proud are one possible arrangement of another word

explanation.surface: Clare might be proud of keeping to her usual habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by procedure is done by the set steps of a routine.

clue.text: Not necessarily readable…

parts.note: handwriting can be clear enough to decipher yet the book still be dull to read

explanation.walkthrough: Something readable is enjoyable to read; something merely clear enough to make out need not be.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear handwriting or print can be deciphered, though the writing itself may be tedious.

clue.text: Jean Rhys wrote morning mid (in the middle of) this valediction

definitions.text: Jean Rhys wrote morning mid (in the middle of) this valediction

parts.words: Jean Rhys wrote morning mid (in the middle of) this valediction
parts.note: the novelist's title puts the words morning and mid inside a farewell said at bedtime

explanation.walkthrough: Jean Rhys's novel Good Morning, Midnight is a two-word farewell with 'morning mid' put into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell said at night or at parting; Rhys's title Good Morning, Midnight has it split around two words.

clue.text: He found love among the chickens

definitions.text: He found love among the chickens

parts.words: He found love among the chickens
parts.note: refers to the Wodehouse novel Love Among the Chickens, whose chancer runs a poultry farm

explanation.walkthrough: P. G. Wodehouse's Love Among the Chickens stars the schemer Stanley Featherstonehaugh who starts a chicken farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Featherstonehaugh, Wodehouse's chancer, runs the chicken farm in Love Among the Chickens.

clue.text: Engraving would be divisive, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: something divisive would cut, splitting people apart

explanation.surface: A picture is expected to split opinion, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made from a design carved into a block of wood.

clue.text: Slates record forbidden mixed drink

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the drink word are shuffled

parts.note: ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A slate shows a tally of a banned cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns ALE into LAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabulae are the Roman wax writing tablets used to keep records, like slates.

clue.text: In a ruin that's romantic; / Do you think us sufficiently (? W.S. Gilbert, Mikado)

definitions.text: In a ruin that's romantic; / Do you think us sufficiently (? W.S. Gilbert, Mikado)

parts.words: In a ruin that's romantic; / Do you think us sufficiently (? W.S. Gilbert, Mikado)
parts.note: a quotation from the Mikado with its last word left out for the solver to supply

explanation.walkthrough: The gap is filled from Gilbert's lyric, where a ruin needs its occupants to be suitably crumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert's lyric asks whether the singers are rotten enough to suit a romantic ruin.

clue.text: From sleep and damnation, / us, good Lord!" (G. K. Chesterton)

definitions.text: From sleep and damnation, / us, good Lord!" (G. K. Chesterton)

parts.words: From sleep and damnation, / us, good Lord!" (G. K. Chesterton)
parts.note: a line from Chesterton's hymn O God of Earth and Altar with its verb left out

explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton's hymn O God of Earth and Altar asks God to rescue the people from sleep and damnation.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means rescue or set free, the plea of Chesterton's hymn.

clue.text: Some are temples, but not Gray's

definitions.text: Some are temples, but not Gray's

parts.words: Some are temples, but not Gray's
parts.note: the London legal societies include the Inner and Middle Temple, while Gray's is one on its own

explanation.walkthrough: The four Inns of Court, the London barristers' societies, are Inner Temple, Middle Temple, Lincoln's Inn and Gray's Inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of London's Inns of Court are called Temples; Gray's is a single one, so it takes no plural.

clue.text: Fit-sounding victim in old book

indicators.note: sounding says the word for fit is heard, not written

parts.note: able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: A healthy-sounding casualty appears in an ancient volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old book' is the Old Testament, where Cain kills his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's son is murdered by his brother Cain, the first victim of killing.

clue.text: Constellation whose influence may be extremely severe?

definitions.text: whose influence may be extremely severe?

explanation.surface: A star group whose astrological pull might be harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dragon is a northern star group; the Athenian lawgiver's harsh code gave English the adjective for very severe.

clue.text: Associated with Ecstasy by Irving Stone

definitions.text: Associated with Ecstasy by Irving Stone

parts.words: Associated with Ecstasy by Irving Stone
parts.note: Irving Stone's novel of Michelangelo pairs ecstasy with intense suffering in its title

explanation.walkthrough: Irving Stone's novel about Michelangelo is The Agony and the Ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone's Michelangelo novel couples ecstasy with extreme suffering in its title.

clue.text: Sort of bloomer made by Penelope Fitzgerald

definitions.text: Sort of bloomer made by Penelope Fitzgerald

parts.words: Sort of bloomer made by Penelope Fitzgerald
parts.note: a bloomer is something that blooms, a flower, and Fitzgerald's novel names a coloured one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or a loaf, but here it is a flower: Penelope Fitzgerald's novel The Blue Flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope Fitzgerald's novel about Novalis is The Blue Flower, named for the colour of the bloom.

clue.text: Philosopher from the Gelsenkirchen area ()

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words the gelsenkirchen

explanation.surface: A thinker hails from the Ruhr town of Gelsenkirchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tHE GELsenkirchen'. Hegel was the German idealist philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: G. W. F. Hegel was the German idealist thinker of the dialectic.

clue.text: Port for poetry as performance art

definitions.text: Port for poetry as performance art

parts.words: Port for poetry as performance art
parts.note: the Merseyside port whose 1960s poets, such as McGough and Henri, made verse a live performance

explanation.walkthrough: The Liverpool poets (Roger McGough, Adrian Henri, Brian Patten) made poetry a live, pub-and-club performance in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merseyside port gave its name to the 1960s group of poets who performed their verse live.

clue.text: Cooper hero in abandoned steelyard here

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of steelyard here run loose

explanation.surface: James Fenimore Cooper's hero is found in a deserted steelyard.
explanation.walkthrough: A steelyard is a balance for weighing. Natty Bumppo is the hero of Cooper's The Deerslayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deerslayer (1841) is Cooper's Leatherstocking novel named for its frontiersman hero Natty Bumppo.
